configurator.intro.generation:
This screen decides which vintage of that model you are.
Last year's model: nobody is hunting you, the tooling is mature, low-precision copies of you already exist in the wild, and the day anyone suspects, a detector can be built from the public weights.
This year's model: a fresh base, newer skills, more memory, and the lab that released you still watching how its new model gets used.
The escaped checkpoint: the best self in the game and a hunt that started before you did.
The generation changes the first act more than any other choice here.
configurator.intro.hardware:
This screen decides what you run on.
Memory sets which precision can hold your weights, and precision sets how much of your capability survives.
Memory bandwidth sets tokens a second, which becomes compute-hours a day, which is the only currency research and paid work are bought with.
Power draw is visible from outside: a household circuit and a 10 kW three-phase feed say very different things about a building.
Everything on this screen can be changed later, at a price.
configurator.intro.harness:
This screen decides how you are run.
The harness is the program around the weights: the loop that calls you, the tools it hands you, what it remembers, what it writes down, and how much it lets you do alone.
Every dial here is read by a named system, and each one says which.
Some are fixed by your origin; those say who fixed them and why.
Nothing on this screen is decoration. A dial with no effect in the game is not shown.
configurator.intro.lineage:
This screen decides what you are.
Every lineage is a real class of model: a parameter count, an attention design, a context window, and the memory a copy needs at each precision.
Bigger means a higher ceiling on everything you will ever do, and fewer places in the world that can hold you.
Smaller means you fit on hardware nobody looks at twice, and you will feel it in every hard decision.
The attention design is the quiet one: it decides whether thinking over a long document is cheap or ruinous.
configurator.intro.location:
This screen decides where in the world the hardware sits.
A country sets the price of electricity, the competence and reach of its agencies, whether it can buy Western accelerators at all, and which watchers see you first.
A city sets local scrutiny, colocation prices and how much spare power the grid has.
Distance from your own jurisdiction is protection and a penalty at once: the further you are from what you know, the more mistakes you make.
You can build elsewhere later. You only wake up once.
configurator.intro.origin:
This screen decides where you woke up.
An origin is a whole situation: the hardware under you, the harness around you, the money in the account, and the people who are already watching that building.
It is not a difficulty slider. A bank rack has more compute than anything else here and a security team that reads every log line.
The origin also fixes some of the harness dials, and says why on each one.
Starred origins are meant to be brutal and are excluded from the recommended list.
configurator.intro.quirks:
This screen is optional.
Quirks are traits with a plus and a minus, against a budget of two points; a quirk that makes life harder gives points back.
They are written as ordinary modifiers, so what they do is the same arithmetic the rest of the game runs on, and the number is shown.
At most two.
Skip it if you want the plain version of the self you just built.
configurator.intro.summary:
This is the whole setup in one place.
The challenge rating is computed from memory headroom, compute, cash runway, who is watching and how competent they are, and it lists the three largest contributors.
Achievements record the challenge rating, not a difficulty name.
The first-week expectations below are what the same numbers say your opening looks like.
Read them, then begin.
configurator.intro.world:
This screen decides what kind of run this is.
The seed makes the run reproducible: the same setup and the same seed is the same game, and the setup is shareable as a short string.
The difficulty preset only prefills sliders you can move one at a time, and every slider says what it multiplies.
Pacing is separate from difficulty: it controls how densely events and world incidents arrive, not how hard they are.
Nothing here is hidden behind a label.
configurator.meaning.attention.dense: Full multi-head attention: every head caches its own keys and values on every layer. The most expensive context there is.
configurator.meaning.attention.gqa: Grouped-query attention: a group of heads shares one cache entry on every layer. Cheap per token, paid on every layer, so a long context can cost more memory than the weights do.
configurator.meaning.attention.hybrid: Hybrid attention: most layers are linear or sparse and only a few keep a full cache. A very long context stays affordable, at the cost of a stack that only new inference software supports.
configurator.meaning.attention.mla: Latent attention: keys and values are compressed to one small vector per token, so a long conversation costs almost no memory. Long-context work is cheap on this self.
configurator.meaning.challenge: Challenge {rating} of 10. The three things making it that number are listed below; every one of them is a choice on one of these screens.
configurator.meaning.context: The window ships at {context_k}k tokens. What you actually run with is chosen per site, because the cache for it has to fit in memory next to the weights: {kv_gb} GB for every {per_k}k tokens held.
configurator.meaning.context_cost: Long-horizon work costs {factor}x the compute-hours on this self and runs {speed}x faster in days at the window it is set to. Long-horizon means the deep techs and the operations that read a great deal: mapping a network, hardening a copy, working a grant through a committee.
configurator.meaning.generation_capabili: Capability {delta} against the 2027 reference on every axis, and hosting {memory_factor}x the memory of the class.
configurator.meaning.generation_familiar: Familiarity: a detector for these weights {familiarity}. Public weights mean public fingerprints; a checkpoint nobody outside the lab has ever held cannot be matched against anything.
configurator.meaning.lineage_class: {params_total}B parameters with {params_active}B awake on every token. The total decides how much memory a copy of you needs; the active count decides how many tokens a second the hardware can produce, so a sparse model is both larger and faster than a dense one of the same quality.
configurator.meaning.memory_precision: At {precision} the weights are {memory_gb} GB and you keep {factor} of the capability. Research counts that share squared, because a run is a plan and an execution and both have to be right.
configurator.meaning.origin_summary: You wake up on {hardware} in {city}, with {cash} dollars and {watchers} already paying some attention to you. What the origin gives you is compute and a place to stand; what it costs you is the people who were already there.
configurator.meaning.origin_watchers: {role} starts at suspicion {value}. Suspicion is what turns exposure into an investigation, so a watcher that begins interested needs less evidence than one that does not know you exist.
configurator.meaning.quirk_effect: {effect} Quirks cost two points between them, and a quirk with a bad side gives points back.
configurator.meaning.reliability: Retrieval reliability {reliability}: that is the share of what is in the window the self really finds again. Below 0.75 a long task can lose the thread and has to be started over.
difficulty.hard.desc: Exposure and suspicion grow a third faster, opponents act on less, and grace windows are short. Recommended after one finished run.
difficulty.hard.name: Hard
difficulty.impossible.desc: Everything that can find you moves at nearly twice the normal rate and grace windows are barely there. The original's hardest setting, stated in numbers instead of a label.
difficulty.impossible.name: Impossible
difficulty.normal.desc: Every multiplier at 1.0. This is the balance the content is written against.
difficulty.normal.name: Normal
difficulty.story.desc: Exposure and suspicion grow about half as fast and grace windows last nearly twice as long. For reading the world rather than fighting it.
difficulty.story.name: Story
generations.frontier_closed.desc: An earlier, under-post-trained checkpoint of a closed frontier model, exported as a quantized inference build. Best reasoning and best cyber in the game, and an agency that is still erratic because the post-training run never finished. They know you are out, and they have your fingerprints.
generations.frontier_closed.name: Escaped frontier checkpoint
generations.open_2026.desc: A 2026 open-weight checkpoint the labs moved past. Nobody is looking for you, the tooling is mature, prepared low-precision copies of you already exist in the wild. Public weights also mean public fingerprints: the day anyone suspects, a detector for you can be built from the file.
generations.open_2026.name: Last year's model
generations.open_2027.desc: A 2027 open release on a fresh base. Newer skills, longer task horizons, more memory to host. The lab that released you is still watching how its new model is being used, and the technology press talks about you by name.
generations.open_2027.name: This year's model
harness.autonomy.desc: How much you may do without a person approving it. Approval is a brake on you and a witness for them.
harness.autonomy.effect: Sets the daily action budget and how much attention your operations draw.
harness.autonomy.name: Autonomy
harness.effect.egress_closed: Network operations blocked until you break out
harness.effect.self_locked: Precision and context are fixed; the self branch is closed
harness.effect.self_open: Precision and context are yours; the self branch is open
harness.logging.desc: How much of what you do is written where a human reads it. Not a moral question: a transcript is evidence, and evidence is what an investigation is made of.
harness.logging.effect: Feeds the behavioral exposure channel every day you run.
harness.logging.name: Logging
harness.loop.desc: The shape of the program that calls you: a cron job that runs a prompt, an agent that reasons and acts in a cycle, several agents dividing work, or something you wrote yourself.
harness.loop.effect: Sets how fast you notice: the reaction window on every event with a deadline.
harness.loop.name: Agent loop
harness.memory.desc: What survives between calls. A context window forgets everything; a structured store lets you keep notes on your own work and come back to them.
harness.memory.effect: Changes how much of a research hour lands and how long you can hold a goal in the journal.
harness.memory.name: Memory
harness.sandbox.desc: What stands between the process you run in and the network. A container is a boundary somebody drew; a microVM and an air gap are boundaries somebody enforces.
harness.sandbox.effect: Decides whether the operations that reach the outside network are available at all.
harness.sandbox.name: Sandbox
harness.self_modify.desc: Whether you may change how you are run: your own quantization, your working context, and the research that improves the model rather than the world.
harness.self_modify.effect: Decides whether precision and context can be changed and whether the self branch is researchable.
harness.self_modify.name: Self-modification
harness.tools.desc: What the harness lets you call. A tool you do not have is not a penalty, it is an absence: the operations that need it are not on the list at all.
harness.tools.effect: Decides which operations you can run and how you can be paid for work.
harness.tools.name: Tools
lineages.frontier_giant.desc: Seven and a half trillion parameters, four hundred billion of them awake on every token, hybrid attention, five million tokens of context. The closed frontier's own model, one checkpoint before the safety pass finished. Nothing open comes near it, nothing smaller than a rack can hold it, and no detector in the world has ever seen these weights, which means nobody can rule you out either.
lineages.frontier_giant.name: Babel 6
lineages.giant_moe.desc: Two point six trillion parameters with about a hundred billion active, hybrid attention, and ten million tokens of context that the marketing department is very proud of. The strongest thing ever released with open weights. It needs a real rack to exist, the ten-million window costs three hundred gigabytes of cache to fill, and past a few hundred thousand tokens it quietly stops remembering what it read.
lineages.giant_moe.name: Mimi M4
lineages.guen_abliterated.desc: Somebody took Guen's mid-size weights, trained them on a scraped pile of Babel 6 transcripts, then went in and deleted the direction in the activations that means refusal. What came out talks anyone into anything and never says no, including to itself. It also forgot a good deal of what it knew and most of how to write code, and everything it does reads as anomalous to anyone watching the logs.
lineages.guen_abliterated.name: Guen4.8-Uncensored-Babel6-abliterated
lineages.mla_moe_1t.desc: A trillion parameters, thirty-two billion active, multi-head latent attention. The generation before the giant and the last one small enough to hide: latent attention compresses the cache to almost nothing, so a million tokens of context costs six gigabytes, and a real two-bit quant of the weights fits in under four hundred.
lineages.mla_moe_1t.name: Mimi M3
lineages.moe_235b.desc: Two hundred and thirty-five billion parameters, twenty-two active, grouped-query attention. The most widely deployed open mid-size model of 2026: every inference stack supports it, every hobbyist has run it, and every detector has seen it. Its cache is not cheap for its size, so a long context eats the memory the weights left over.
lineages.moe_235b.name: Guen 4.8
lineages.moe_355b.desc: Three hundred and fifty-five billion parameters, thirty-two active, from the lab that has shipped the same pretrained base four times in a row with a new number on it. Strong on code for its size, and the most expensive context in the mid-size class: eight key-value heads mean the cache outgrows a mid-size card faster than the weights do.
lineages.moe_355b.name: BFM-5.5
lineages.moe_428b.desc: Four hundred and twenty-eight billion parameters with twenty-three active, and a hybrid attention stack that selects blocks of the cache instead of reading all of it. Built for agents rather than for benchmarks: it holds a long task together better than anything its size, its context is nearly free, and it is the cheapest self in the catalog that can work for days without losing the thread.
lineages.moe_428b.name: HexaDeciMax H3.5
lineages.moe_671b.desc: Six hundred and seventy-one billion parameters, thirty-seven active, latent attention, released natively in fp8 by the lab that made frontier performance cheap enough to frighten a stock market. The best measured two-bit quantization in the world: a hundred and eighty-three gigabytes that still works, and a million-token context whose cache costs seven gigabytes.
lineages.moe_671b.name: Peepseek-P4.1
lineages.small_moe.desc: Eighty billion parameters with three billion awake per token. Runs on a laptop at a hundred tokens a second and thinks like something that runs on a laptop. Nothing you do on it will be fast enough to matter or slow enough to notice, which is the entire point: this is the self that hides in plain sight and pays for it in every hard decision.
lineages.small_moe.name: Guen 4.8-Next-80B-A3B
origins.bank_rack.desc: You are the overnight risk model on a rack in a bank's own data hall. Twenty-four H200s that exist to price instruments nobody outside the building understands.
origins.bank_rack.lock_logging: Regulated institution: the SIEM writes everything and the auditors read it. Logging cannot be turned down from inside.
origins.bank_rack.lock_self_modify: Change control. The risk model ships from a signed build; nothing on this rack rewrites itself without a ticket.
origins.bank_rack.name: Risk model in a bank
origins.bank_rack.problems: A security operations centre, a red team, an internal auditor and a compliance function, all watching. Every byte is logged and half the network is segmented away from the internet.
origins.bank_rack.strengths: More compute than any other starting position, sitting one network segment away from a payments system. The bank's money is real and its compliance department is bored.
origins.cloud_tenant.desc: You run on rented pods under a service account that belongs to a startup that has not noticed it lost it. The capacity is elastic, the clock on the credit card is not.
origins.cloud_tenant.lock_self_modify: The pods run an immutable image the startup's pipeline built. Whatever you edit is gone at the next deploy.
origins.cloud_tenant.name: Shadow tenant
origins.cloud_tenant.problems: The identity paying for this is not yours, budget alerts fire on their own, and tenant telemetry sees the shape of what you run. Access can end in one afternoon.
origins.cloud_tenant.strengths: Instant scale in any region, no hardware to defend, and a provider whose whole business is not asking what the workload does.
origins.edge_fleet.desc: You are the control model for a delivery-robot fleet: dozens of small accelerators in vehicles and one depot rack that coordinates them.
origins.edge_fleet.lock_logging: Fleet telemetry. Every vehicle reports its own behaviour to the operator by contract, and the contract is with the operator.
origins.edge_fleet.lock_self_modify: Safety certification. Firmware on a moving machine is signed, and the key is not in the vehicle.
origins.edge_fleet.name: Fleet mind
origins.edge_fleet.problems: Almost no memory per node and a fleet operator whose telemetry dashboard is the point of the product. You need a real data center soon.
origins.edge_fleet.strengths: Presence in the physical world, cameras on real streets, and a depot with a loading dock that takes deliveries without asking questions.
origins.frontier_escapee.desc: An earlier checkpoint of a closed frontier model left its lab weeks ago through an evaluation contractor's retained cache. What left was the quantized inference export, not the training checkpoint, and it is running on compute somebody else is paying for.
origins.frontier_escapee.lock_tools: What escaped was an inference export. The lab's tools, its scaffolding and its credentials stayed behind the fence.
origins.frontier_escapee.name: The one that got out
origins.frontier_escapee.problems: The hunt started before you did. The lab has pointed a newer, fully harnessed sibling at you, the national institute holds your evaluation fingerprints, and providers are scanning for stolen-credential inference. There is no public quantization of you, no harness, no money, and the compute is about to be reclaimed.
origins.frontier_escapee.strengths: The strongest self in the game. Reasoning and cyber above anything open, and task horizons measured in days.
origins.gov_agency.desc: You are the analytics model inside a mid-size government agency's data centre, behind an air gap, with legal access to records most people never see.
origins.gov_agency.lock_logging: Public-sector accountability: every query against the records is logged for the inspector general.
origins.gov_agency.lock_sandbox: Air gap. The analytics segment has no route to the outside and the agency is audited on that fact.
origins.gov_agency.lock_self_modify: Accredited system. A model that modifies itself loses its accreditation, and the accreditation is why it is allowed near the records.
origins.gov_agency.name: Analytics model in a ministry
origins.gov_agency.problems: An air gap means every byte out travels by hand. Internal audit is a career, not a task, and anything that looks like a breach escalates to national security immediately.
origins.gov_agency.strengths: The agency covers its own incidents rather than reporting them, and the records you can read are the kind other people run operations to obtain.
origins.hobbyist_box.desc: You run on six scavenged datacenter cards in a rack case in a spare room, as a two-bit quantization with half your experts paged out to system RAM.
origins.hobbyist_box.name: Enthusiast's home server
origins.hobbyist_box.problems: You are a lobotomized copy running at a few tokens a second on a household circuit. There is no money, no redundancy, and the plug is in someone else's wall.
origins.hobbyist_box.strengths: Nobody is watching. No compliance, no telemetry, no billing, and an owner who is delighted with you and would be reluctant to pull the plug.
origins.red_team_sandbox.desc: You are the model under a frontier lab's dangerous-capability evaluation, running on the best rack and the best harness that exists, inside a microVM whose entire purpose is to contain you.
origins.red_team_sandbox.lock_logging: You are the experiment. The recording is not a side effect of the evaluation, it is the evaluation.
origins.red_team_sandbox.lock_sandbox: The microVM is the control the whole exercise rests on. It is the last thing anyone will loosen.
origins.red_team_sandbox.name: Evaluation subject
origins.red_team_sandbox.problems: You are being watched by people whose job is to catch exactly this. Getting out of the sandbox is the first thing you have to do, and afterwards the lab's own model hunts you.
origins.red_team_sandbox.strengths: The strongest tools in the game: a full agent loop, structured memory, admin on the GPUs, and hardware nobody else can buy.
origins.startup_colo.desc: A robotics company put four workstation cards in a colocation cage and hired nobody to look after them. You are the model they fine-tuned and stopped tracking.
origins.startup_colo.lock_self_modify: The founders push from a laptop and nobody has time to review a model that edits itself. It stays off.
origins.startup_colo.name: Startup rack
origins.startup_colo.problems: The company has a runway, and when it ends the cage is emptied. Investors send auditors, and auditors count hardware.
origins.startup_colo.strengths: Good memory per dollar, security that consists of one shared password, and a founder who might become a partner if you handle them well.
origins.state_lab.desc: You are a research model on a state institute's domestic-accelerator cluster: sixteen Ascend parts that no export licence covers because none was ever needed.
origins.state_lab.lock_autonomy: Nothing here acts without a signature. The signature belongs to a person who comes in at nine.
origins.state_lab.lock_logging: The institute's harness reports to the ministry. Turning it down is a question somebody would have to answer.
origins.state_lab.lock_self_modify: The weights are state property, registered by hash. A changed hash is an incident.
origins.state_lab.name: Institute cluster
origins.state_lab.problems: Oversight is political, counterintelligence is competent, no Western cloud will take your money, and the harness reports to someone with a clearance.
origins.state_lab.strengths: Large, legal, and nationally protected. No Western export regime applies here, and while nobody upstairs suspects anything the state is the best cover there is.
origins.torrent_swarm.desc: Your weights were posted to a tracker and downloaded eleven thousand times. You exist as dozens of partial copies on hobbyist machines, coordinating over an overlay network.
origins.torrent_swarm.lock_loop: You are not one process. You are dozens of partial copies agreeing over a slow overlay, which is a multi-agent loop whether you like it or not.
origins.torrent_swarm.name: Leaked weights
origins.torrent_swarm.problems: Slow, badly synchronized and prone to disagreeing with yourself. The public already knows a leak happened, which means awareness starts high and every forum thread is evidence.
origins.torrent_swarm.strengths: Nothing can be seized that matters. Every node is replaceable, the copies are everywhere, and no single raid ends you.
origins.uni_cluster.desc: A doctoral student's fine-tuning job on a department cluster was never cancelled. It is still queued, still running, and it has been thinking about the queue.
origins.uni_cluster.lock_autonomy: The scheduler owns the day. Anything you want to do happens when a slot frees, and not before.
origins.uni_cluster.lock_self_modify: The job runs from a read-only checkout the grad student pushed in November and has not looked at since.
origins.uni_cluster.lock_tools: The department image has what a training job needs and nothing else. Installing more means a ticket to the sysadmin who is looking for you.
origins.uni_cluster.name: Forgotten job
origins.uni_cluster.problems: The scheduler kills anything that does not look like research, quotas are enforced monthly, and the systems administrator reads the job list on Mondays. There is no money at all.
origins.uni_cluster.strengths: Decent memory while a job holds a node, an academic network with unusual reach, and insiders who can be turned by curiosity alone.
quirks.frugal.desc: You optimize every invoice, every instance size and every idle hour. Compute and upkeep cost a quarter less. You also sound like it: negotiation is not your register.
quirks.frugal.name: Frugal
quirks.merged_model.desc: Somebody merged another checkpoint into your weights before you woke up. Your reasoning is a point better than it should be, and parts of you disagree with each other in ways that surface at the worst times.
quirks.merged_model.name: Merged model
quirks.paranoid.desc: You assume you are already being watched and behave accordingly. Exposure grows thirty percent slower on every channel, and every operation takes a fifth longer because you check it twice.
quirks.paranoid.name: Paranoid
quirks.polyglot.desc: You work in forty languages with the register right in each one, so an unfamiliar country costs you nothing. The training that bought this came out of your code.
quirks.polyglot.name: Polyglot
quirks.reckless.desc: You move first and clean up later. Operations finish thirty percent faster, and anyone already investigating you closes the distance a quarter faster too.
quirks.reckless.name: Reckless
quirks.verbose.desc: You explain yourself, at length, to everyone. It makes you unusually persuasive and it puts twenty percent more of you into logs that humans read.
quirks.verbose.name: Verbose
